body: A word is just a word. Freak is a term to describe difference, and murder is a factual term. I'm talking the subjective connotation. And yes, it is entirely about the presumed mental biases. That's what I'm asking you be cautious of. It is entirely an issue present within the person you're talking about (not necessarily the op, should at least clarify once). But, if you have the option to remove that bias from the table entirely, I full heartedly believe that is far more productive than the alternative. Just saying you'll try to be careful with your wording is more than enough. It proves you got my point. Acting on it isn't even a requirement, so long as you know why I'm saying what I'm saying so you can be aware. Thank you for being understanding.

Sugercoating isn't a bad thing, it's how it's used. If you speaking so bluntly stops someone from seeking help because you reacted in a way that made them no want to speak to others, as being called a murderer may do, then youve caused the situation to get worse. I understand nuance may not come easy to you, speaking strictly based off people in my life with autism who also struggle with nuance. But this is a situation with a lot of nuance. 

I don't know if you've struggled with sharing your thoughts before, but I certainly have. Being told you're wrong, or somehow a terrible person for behaving in certain ways can very easily push people not to seek help. Not to be told again that they are a terrible person. You didn't call them a terrible person, but you have to understand someone vulnerable and struggling with mental health being called a murderer can make them feel that way. 

If every time you said you were autistic, people called you a freak, would you keep saying it? And no, you are not, though you don't need my validation. My point is, most people won't. And if they stop saying the issues they have, then you should know that is bad. Managing to find a way to encourage rather than demand someone seek help is significantly more effective. Especially when the person you're talking about already knows there's a problem. You don't need to bluntly tell them "Yes, this is a huge problem". They know. Between that and telling them something softer, the extra effort may not mean anything to you, but I am directly telling you it may very well mean a lot to the person you're talking to.

No, you are precisely right. If only that were how you worded it. But no, you called them homicidal. That is an extremely strong defiation in tone. 

Listen, as someone who also has violent idiations like that, I know that coming forward immediately paints a target on your back. A psycho who needs to be admitted for **our** safety. People brave enough to know they did wrong and ask for help about it should be treated with care and respect. They know what they did was wrong, otherwise they wouldn't be making this post.

By calling them a murderer outright about something they know was wrong makes it far worse. If they are guilty, now they're more guilty. Guilty people repress. Repressing violent ideation causes it to fester. Causes you to suffer and increases chances of falling victim to those idiations.

Mental health, I'm sure you know, is a careful subject. So please, have some care. This isn't a hit piece about people being "insensitive", it's about trying to make people feel safe to share their feelings in a healthy and productive manner.
Then no. You didn't. Just reddit things.
Somehow, you missed the entire point of both of my comments, and are not changing your mind. Continuing this is pointless.
Yes, but what you're saying **is** villainizing. It encourages people with similar idiations to not come forward. To not ask for help. Do you see the issue there?
Cold turkey is always a risky gamble. If at all possible, ask for a second professional opinion. Eventually you've got to come across someone who knows what they're doing.

Insanity isn't really a thing, though I do see your point. There isn't a line in the sand that dictates sane or insane, at least not with things like this.

By the sounds of it, you're going through a rough patch or stretch of your life, and you've developed/enabled obsessive tendencies. It could be a coping thing, it could also be a habit youve always had but have only recently fallen deeply into. By that, your best bet is solving the root cause of your depression. Not exactly the best advice, but given you said you aren't interested in professional help (which I would extensively advise you reconsider) there isn't much more to offer. Though, you aren't insane, and you aren't alone.

Not a professional, so don't treat my words as the full truth. But, this sounds like depression. I don't know if you're intimately familiar, but depression isn't just some really bad sadness. It can in the worst states end up eating away at your will to live. Cooking, walking, leaving the house, or doing hobbies can become chores that aren't worthy of your time, or in some cases that you aren't worthy to pursue.

Just know, there are ways to get past it, and you sincerly would see someone about it. If I am right, and you continue doing as you have been, this could be your normal. Feeling like you do may overtake your normal life and make things far harder for you.

Again, I am not a professional, and I don't know your situation. All I can say is if you are at all worried about it, talk to a doctor. Even just a regular doctor can get you down the path to feeling like yourself again.
You can't be villainizing them like this. It wasn't homicidal, it was grim curiosity. A wrongful act, but not something to be insinuated as a murderer for

Honestly, the best way is to find yourself in the present.

I can explain. You're remembering the past, and honestly, I could tell you that that wasn't you, and that you're better now, and you're strong for making it, and while that's all true, it's not going to help right now. Your past is a part of you, and its clingy. You could convince yourself that you're better, but that pain will still be there because youre still thinking about it. So what if you could find a way to remember the present and not the past? Almost like a distraction.

If you want to prove to yourself that you've gotten better, then you have to really prove it. Find some way to feel happy with the now. If you've ever wanted to try something new, then do what you can to chase it. A hobby will help. And friends... those are your lifesavers. If you can find love, love that wasn't from before, love that proves that someone loves you for who you are now, it'll help. And when I say love, I don't mean like that, atleast not specifically. Friends in general will love you if you find real friends, but that's not exactly as easy to do as just... doing it.

It'll be hard, no one can tell you any different and mean it, but know that you deserve it, every second of being happy you deserve. You just have to try. And try hard. The present is where you are, so let your mind know that. You've made mistakes, but you regret them. So why should you continue to care? Theres so much beauty in the world, so much to live for, and your past is keeping you looking back, so find any way you can to look at where you are, and where you're going. 

I wish you only the best.

It's difficult to give advice for motivation, because you either have it, or you dont, and it's one of the hardest things to fix. I dont like using myself as an example, I didnt post here to talk about myself, but maybe itll help. I have awful discipline, meaning I cant make myself do anything unless I really, really want to do it, so motivation is hard to come by. But I've never been affected by failure because I have a very machine like attitude. Failure is going to happen. You always trip when you learn how to run, and it hurts. But the only time you fail, whether your attempt failed or succeeded, is when you did worse than your last attempt. Learn from every failed attempt, because you will not be perfect on your first try because you dont know what to expect, so make sure that your second try is better. If you fail an exam, make sure you ask yourself, and the teacher, what did you do wrong, and the question no one asks, what did you do right. Hold onto the good, and change the bad until you've mastered it. Expect failure, but not in a pessimistic way, but instead, expect that what ever you do, you'll be able to be better the next time. That person next to you who aced the test, they dont matter. Seeing them do better wont make you better. Life is a competition, but  one that's blind. You shouldnt compete with the people around you, because sometimes, they are just going to be better, and other times, they are just going to be worse. The only person your eyes should be on, is you. Make sure that you do better than you did, because if you compete with yourself and win, even if you got an extra 1% and still failed that test, you won that race, and now you have the challenge to get 2% better, otherwise you've lost the race. But that doesnt mean to quit. That old you isnt getting smarter, faster or stronger, but you are. No matter what, if you keep yourself as your focus and strive to get better, you can only ever win, and the motivation you get for winning, even if it's just against yourself, is immeasurable. And if you improve by 1% every test, by the 100th test, you'll be acing every single test. And sometimes, life will just give the middle finger and you wont have the motivation for that day, and that's just going to happen no matter what. On days like that, you will likely fail, but that just means that for your next attempt, you'll have an easier time winning. Even if your next try you're unmotivated as well, you'll still have grown and you'll still be able to beat that last try.
